data.gender_notes: Deenabandhu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is a friend or helper to the gods. The name Deenabandhu is derived from two Sanskrit words: 'deena' meaning 'gods' and 'bandhu' meaning 'friend' or 'helper'. The name Deenabandhu carries the meaning “Friend of the Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Deenabandhu usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes devotion and a deep connection to the divine.
data.etymology: Deenabandhu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of the Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Deenabandhu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It emphasizes the concept of being devoted to and serving the deities, a fundamental aspect of Hindu spirituality and culture. Moreover, the name celebrates the idea of seeking the blessings and protection of the gods.

Ultimately, Deenabandhu signifies the journey towards enlightenment through the grace and guidance of the deities.

historical_references.reference: Deenabandhu was a prominent Bengali Hindu leader and poet who was an active participant in the Indian freedom struggle. He was born in 1896 in the village of Kantal in Birbhum, West Bengal. He joined the Indian National Congress in 1920 and became a prominent figure in the non-cooperation movement led by Mahatma Gandhi. He was arrested several times for his involvement in the freedom struggle. After India's independence, he served as a Member of Parliament from West Bengal.

Deenabandhu Mukherjee was a noted Bengali poet, writer, and social reformer. He was born in 1896 in the village of Kantal in Birbhum, West Bengal. He was deeply influenced by the works of Rabindranath Tagore and Kazi Nazrul Islam. He wrote poetry that reflected the social and political realities of his time, often focusing on the plight of the common man. His most famous works include 'Hariprasad Chhaterjee', 'Banglar Mati', and 'Deenabandhu Samajpatra'.
